purpose: Validates and routes every supervisor reply and drives generation I/O/deadline tasks.
behavior: Gen::read buffers partial frames, rejects EOF mid-frame and unaccounted descriptors, and propagates malformed-frame errors from omni-proto::decode.
Gen::route requires Ready first and compares its version with VERSION. Replies must match request kind and tree ID; reused tree IDs and duplicate exits end the generation.
Waiters are removed only after validation; life notifications and reply delivery occur outside the lock. Earliest missed asynchronous deadline kills the generation.
contracts: Descriptors ride the first byte of their frame and are cleared after a positive send.
Exited for a forgotten tree is ignored.
dependencies: omni-proto::decode validates framing and extracts message fields, including the transmitted Ready version; omni-proto::VERSION supplies the expected version for the separate comparison in Gen::route.
client/channel.rs owns pending requests, trees and death propagation.
failures_or_limits: Ack is accepted for any non-Spawn request after ID validation; caller-level methods interpret the result.

purpose: Serializes the Unix PTY Go handshake across competing callers.
behavior: Held transitions to Sending for one sender; concurrent callers wait on a condvar and then share Done.
A send error means no request was admitted and returns state to Held, allowing retry; an accepted result, including failure, is memoized.
contracts: The waiting caller has a bounded wait and receives a supervisor-refused error if another Go remains in flight.
dependencies: client/mod.rs maps GoEnd into public errors and confirms exec.
failures_or_limits: This helper is synchronous and relies on the supplied send operation being bounded.

purpose: Prepares reaping and identity-based termination of Unix supervisor processes.
behavior: Creates a reaper thread before process creation, then adopts the Child and records an identity before handoff.
On Linux, Ident::adopt opens a pidfd and retains it after live-child /proc and signal-0 checks; the ordinary Watch::kill to Ident::kill path sends SIGKILL through that descriptor.
macOS precreates a kqueue, tracks NOTE_EXIT and records start time; the ordinary Ident::kill path checks the watch and start time immediately before signaling.
Separately, Keeper::adopt handles a failed Child handoff to the reaper by calling Child::kill and Child::wait, ignoring both results, before returning the Watch.
contracts: In the ordinary Watch/Ident kill path, a missing Linux pidfd returns Abandoned. On macOS, a recorded or newly observed exit returns Gone first; otherwise, an absent captured start time returns Abandoned, while a captured start with a missing or different current start time is classified Gone.
dependencies: client/unix.rs owns supervisor startup and delayed close; libc provides pidfd/kqueue APIs.
failures_or_limits: The ordinary macOS Ident::kill path retains a documented check-to-signal PID-reuse window despite its identity checks.

The pidfd-only and identity-based abandonment statements are scoped to the ordinary Watch/Ident path. Keeper::adopt has the separate failed-handoff Child::kill/wait fallback; this file does not establish the standard-library internals of those operations.

purpose: Exposes the private host-side supervisor runtime and generation-bound Tree operations.
behavior: Lazily creates a dedicated multithread Tokio runtime with I/O and time, independent of the caller runtime and checked against creator PID.
spawn uses a shared registry with a 10 s request deadline and 20 s join bound; Unix PTY roots stay held until reader setup and Go.

Tree caches exit via watch state; stop uses cleanup admission and awaits Stopped, and resize is fire-and-forget. processes returns an empty vector immediately when life.gone is set; otherwise, after the loss check, it returns the supervisor's Processes list unchanged, including an empty list.
contracts: Dropping Tree sends Release without waiting; forked copies neither lock nor command the inherited generation.
Generation loss is Io, distinct from a confirmed gone tree.
dependencies: client/channel.rs handles routing, capacity and shared life state.
failures_or_limits: Root exit and whole-tree disappearance are separate facts; Release alone preserves supervisor cleanup duty.

purpose: Serializes lazy supervisor startup, resolves the binary, and transfers launch stdio.
behavior: Concurrent startup joiners share one attempt; later callers retry after failure with a new generation number.

spawn_on builds Spawn from validated Spec, hands pipes to the supervisor and reclaims transferred Windows handles on pre-admission failure; terminal-end adoption failure calls stop_detached(Duration::ZERO) to attempt a detached Stop request, then returns an error without awaiting tree-gone confirmation.
Lookup prioritizes configured path, nonempty environment override, trusted native-module directory, then executable and canonical executable directories.
contracts: The configure cutoff is Registry::started() (num > 0): get increments num before its first open attempt and retains it after a failed attempt; configure_in refuses a different path when that flag is true but accepts the same configured path idempotently.
Unix module candidate and binary must be owned by user/root and not group/other writable.
dependencies: client platform modules implement pipe/handle transfer and module location.
spawn::Spec contains already resolved OS-string inputs.
client/mod.rs::Tree::stop_detached attempts cleanup-request submission without waiting for Stopped.
failures_or_limits: Windows trusted() returns true based on a documented per-user TEMP assumption; it performs no ACL check.

The detached stop returns early outside the home process or when life is gone/lost, and ignores the tell result; this error path establishes neither successful Stop submission nor confirmed tree disappearance.
